The only wave change is inside the second wave: the bootstrap refactor must land before the child agent-id helper and subagent metadata work, because approved plan tasks 3 and 4 both depend on task 2.

tasks._reorder_note: Promoted from Wave C into Wave B because Wave B's first wave review (task-006 attempt 1) found that the live parent hook conflicts with task-003's new bootstrap behavior on the AGENT_LEDGER_TASK_ID env contract. Both sides of the contract must land before Wave B's wave review can pass. Original Wave C parallelism with task-008 is lost; Wave C now contains only task-008.

tasks.description: Make child-mode bootstrap failures fatal in the pi extension.
tasks._reorder_note: Added by Wave B's second wave review (task-006 attempt 2). The prior three critical/important findings closed cleanly, but a new integration bug surfaced: when PI_SUBAGENT_CHILD=1 and bootstrap fails (correct hard-fail per decision 3), the extension's tool_call hook only blocks when AGENT_LEDGER_REQUIRE_TASK=1 or AGENT_LEDGER_TASK_ID is already set. So a misconfigured child whose bootstrap exits non-zero would still execute tool calls without a durable assignment row, violating decision 3 end to end. Fix: treat PI_SUBAGENT_CHILD=1 as mandatory bootstrap enforcement (same gate as AGENT_LEDGER_REQUIRE_TASK=1), and persist eager-bootstrap failure state so the first tool_call returns block:true. Add a matching contract test in run.sh for the PI_SUBAGENT_CHILD=1 + missing-parent-task path.

Wave B's first wave review confirmed that the kernel assign command at internal/commands/assign.go:20-112 already supports distinct --orchestrator and --agent fields, so this audit task remains valuable for regression test coverage but is unlikely to require kernel changes.
